correctness.rationale: When tau(n) is a power of 2, each prime exponent is 2^s-1; sigma_k(p^{2^s-1})=product_{j=0}^{s-1}(p^{k2^j}+1). For even k with t=v2(k), any odd prime ell dividing a factor has v2(ord_ell(p))=t+j+1 and hence v2(ell-1)≥t+1. Therefore every protected odd q with v2(q-1)≤t avoids sigma_k(n) and has valuation k v_q(n) in the reduced denominator. For n,m in F_k, denominator equality recovers their entire odd parts. The remaining factor 2^a is uniquely recoverable since sum_{j=0}^a2^{-kj} strictly increases, including a=0. As 1≤R_k(n)<2 for k≥2, fractional-part injectivity follows. All n=1 and even n included. Read the frozen exact verifier and independently checked bounded cases for five k; finite checks are only corroborating.
